reason: The cited lines show no arbitrary host code execution. They do show local file paths being passed to Puppeteer file-upload mechanisms (`handle.uploadFile(...filePaths)` and `fileChooser.accept(filePaths)`), which can make agent-selected file data available to the current browser page, so these lines support a SINK effect. They do not show file contents or other non-public data being returned into the agent context, only a status line with the paths and an optional snapshot call, so SECRET is not supported. The optional `response.includeSnapshot()` might return page content, but these lines alone do not establish what that snapshot contains or whether it is attacker-controllable, so UNTRUSTED is insufficient.
